### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, the elapsed time between the completion of A16, A17, A18 or A19 and the next completion of A27 sat at a median of about 1.0–1.1 hours; in the later window these medians are about 2.0–2.2 hours. Each of the four transitions shows roughly one extra hour (for example, A16–A27 goes from a median of about 1.0 hours to about 2.1 hours) [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003, TWAIT004].
- The shifts rest on moderate numbers of observed consecutive completion pairs: 36 before vs 64 after for A16–A27, 57 vs 49 for A17–A27, 47 vs 38 for A18–A27, and 60 vs 49 for A19–A27 [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003, TWAIT004].
- The spread of these times also grew: standard deviations rose from about 0.13–0.15 hours to about 0.29–0.33 hours, so in the later window the times are both higher and more variable [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003, TWAIT004].
- Each of the four differences is larger than the difference seen in more than 999 of 1,000 random re-splits of the pooled windows [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003, TWAIT004].
- The signal is confined to timing: the time family produced 4 qualifying items where about 0.01 would be expected without any change, while the control-flow family produced 0 items where about 0.27 were expected, so no structural difference is indicated at these thresholds [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003, TWAIT004].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a timing change centred on A27: in the later window, the elapsed time from the completion of each of A16, A17, A18 and A19 to the next completion of A27 is about twice as long as before, roughly 2 hours instead of roughly 1 hour. The four pair-level measurements agree in direction and magnitude (about +1 hour each), each difference exceeds more than 999 of 1,000 random re-splits, and the time family yielded 4 items against an expectation of about 0.01 without change, so chance alone cannot plausibly account for the set. Control-flow screening found nothing, so this stands as a timing change in its own right, without an observed structural counterpart [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003, TWAIT004].

Limitations: this indicator measures elapsed time between consecutive completion events, not pure waiting or service time, so the extra hour may arise anywhere between the two completions (intervening work, queueing, scheduling) rather than at A27 itself, and the evidence cannot localise it. The observed pair counts also differ between windows (36 vs 64 for A16–A27, small decreases for the others), but no control-flow or ordering item qualified, so any accompanying change in how often these pairs occur is not supported by the evidence [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003, TWAIT004].
